title: Evaluating a Deterministic-Validator Plus Single‑Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=300 intent→configuration tasks, cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) to test whether a guarded pipeline—single-shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini) followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to plain single‑shot generation. Execution (planned episodes 600, completed 600, model_calls_used 301) produced baseline = 299/300 valid configurations (99.667%) and guarded = 300/300 valid configurations (100.0%); paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). A preregistered sensitivity that treats any failed model call as a failure produced identical summary counts because no model-call failures occurred (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in misconfiguration) is not supported: baseline performance was near‑ceiling and the recorded runtime sampling semantics (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") reused the same initial candidate across paired arms, increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing discordant pairs available for McNemar inference. We report the preregistered design, execution accounting, and archived validator/repair traces and discuss statistical, methodological, and operational implications for future, more challenging evaluations.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configurations is central to intent‑driven NetOps, yet misordered or incorrect changes can cause outages or security regressions. Prior work recommends combine‑and‑verify architectures (generation + deterministic validators/simulators ± human approval) and shows verifier‑assisted loops reduce factual errors in related domains. We preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to test a minimal guarded pipeline: a frozen deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair iteration. Research question (preregistered): Can a pipeline combining a frozen deterministic configuration validator and a single automated repair iteration reduce the first‑pass misconfiguration rate of LLM‑generated network configurations relative to plain single‑shot generation on a paired intent→configuration task set? Our contribution is an evidence‑grounded, preregistered paired evaluation (N=300) with full archival of model outputs, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts that quantifies the pipeline's effect under the recorded runtime sampling semantics.
sections.related_work: Recent demonstrations and surveys document LLM‑assisted configuration synthesis and intent translation in constrained settings and recommend verifier‑orchestrated designs for safer NetOps. Studies in other domains show RAG and verifier loops measurably reduce hallucinations and improve grounding; architecture papers advocate generate→verify→repair workflows with deterministic safety nets. However, rigorously preregistered A/B experiments that quantify misconfiguration‑rate reductions from a minimal verifier+single‑repair pipeline in NetOps are sparse. Our experiment situates itself in this gap by providing a preregistered paired test with deterministic task generation and archived validator evidence. Representative prior works cited include intent‑to‑configuration demonstrations and verifier architectures (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 deterministic task seeds and two within‑task conditions: baseline (single‑shot generation) and guarded (same initial generation guarded by a deterministic validator with ≤1 automated repair call). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test: exact McNemar (α=0.05). Model & runtime: declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini; archived model_configuration records temperature = null and generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false, so the same initial sampled candidate was reused across paired arms for each task (this choice isolates validator/repair effects but increases within‑pair correlation). Task bank & scoring: 300 synthetic intent→configuration pairs were deterministically generated (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) with canonical reference answers; a frozen deterministic constraint checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) produced pass/fail scores and validator traces. Execution contract limited each task to one initial generation call and at most one repair call; all raw outputs and traces were archived. The preregistered sensitivity that treats failed model calls as failures was executed; because there were no failed model calls (analysis/missingness_summary.csv), the sensitivity yields identical summary counts to the primary analysis.
sections.results: Execution accounting (archived): planned episodes = 600, completed episodes = 600, complete pairs = 300, model_calls_used = 301; no provider or technical failures occurred and preregistered contamination checks flagged zero tasks. Primary outcomes (archived analysis artifacts): baseline_success_count = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded_success_count = 300/300 (100.0%); paired contingency: n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Absolute paired difference = 0.00333; bootstrap (paired‑percentile) 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair usage: a single repair‑stage call occurred and produced the sole discordant correction; all validator/repair traces are archived. The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in misconfiguration) is not supported because baseline performance was near‑ceiling and the shared_initial_candidate runtime semantics reduced discordant pairs and therefore statistical sensitivity to the preregistered effect size.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and implications: First, on this constrained synthetic task bank and with the tested model/configuration, single‑shot LLM generation achieved near‑ceiling validity; in such regimes even a perfect guard adds little observable relative improvement, although it can deterministically correct isolated failures. Second, sampling semantics matter: reusing a shared initial candidate per pair (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") isolates the validator's corrective effect but increases within‑pair correlation and reduces the number of discordant pairs available to McNemar inference—this interaction should be considered during preregistration and when selecting paired vs. independent draws. Third, observed effect sizes depend critically on task difficulty and validator coverage: stronger operational conclusions require harder or adversarial task suites, broader validator fidelity (e.g., dynamic emulation), multi‑iteration repair, sampling regimes with non‑null temperatures or independent draws, multiple model families, and larger N when baseline pass rates are high. Reproducibility and provenance: all raw responses, per‑task validator traces, repair traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (see execution_manifest.json and analysis artifacts).
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired experiment (N=300) using gpt‑5‑mini and a frozen deterministic validator with ≤1 automated repair iteration, baseline single‑shot generation was near‑ceiling (299/300) and the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs; a single repair call corrected the only observed failure but did not yield a statistically detectable improvement for the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis. The run highlights the need to align preregistered power assumptions and runtime sampling semantics with expected baseline error rates and suggests next steps: evaluate harder/adversarial task banks, broaden validator fidelity (including emulation), allow multi‑iteration repair, vary sampling semantics, and include multiple model families to adequately test operationally meaningful safety hypotheses.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor‑template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

Near‑ceiling baseline performance (299/300) removed headroom to detect the preregistered target effect (≥50% relative reduction); shared_initial_candidate sampling semantics further reduced discordant pairs and statistical sensitivity.

Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; actual runtime consequences of configurations were not executed and remain unmeasured.
